lines.en: In truth, the person I was most worried about was Yoo Joonghyuk.
He was more trustworthy than anyone else here, yet at the same time, I was less certain of him than of anyone else here.
If that lunatic Yoo Joonghyuk shook off my hand and punched me in the face at any moment, everything I was doing now would be utterly pointless.
Fortunately, though, Yoo Joonghyuk remained calm.
Despite the tremendous murderous intent radiating from him, he had surprisingly managed to control his anger and even sent me a secret message.
―What do you think you're doing?
[The character ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ is activating ‘Midday Tryst’.]
······Only then did I remember an item I had bought some time ago.
I had never imagined that the [Midday Tryst] registration from back then would still be valid.
I deliberately answered with shameless confidence.
―I've done this more than once or twice. You should be getting used to it by now.
―What?
―It's not a bad deal for you, either. I know at least that you can't inherit other constellations' ‘Stories’.
Yoo Joonghyuk flinched at my words.
―······I have no idea just how much you know.
In fact, declaring a ‘nebula’ with me was no bad thing for Yoo Joonghyuk at all. If events followed the original novel, he would inherit no Stories here.
That was because of a restriction he had.
[Regressor's Restriction].
In exchange for being able to turn back time through death, he could not inherit other constellations' Stories.
[Incarnation Yoo Joonghyuk. Is what incarnation Kim Dokja says true? The two of you have formed a nebula?]
The dokkaebi hosting the event, who had been watching the situation unfold, intervened.
Everyone turned to Yoo Joonghyuk, and I nervously waited for his answer.
“Yes.”
I let out a sigh of relief.
At any rate, we had cleared the first hurdle.
But the real challenge was only beginning.
Someone burst into laughter amid the audience on the second floor, which had been shrouded in utter silence.
The laughter was gentle and soft, and somehow even cheerful.
Through that laughter, I could feel exactly how Persephone felt.
「Kim Dokja, you've finally done it. This is why I like you.」
Of course I had known she would like it.
Persephone was the sort who went crazy for stories like this.
Following her laughter, the other constellations belatedly began to laugh as well.
Most were constellations on the second floor. Unfortunately, their laughter did not mean the same thing as Persephone's.
[The nebula <Vedas> is disappointed in you.]
[The nebula <Guiok> scorns you.]
Uriel, who had been biting a handkerchief, frowned at the surrounding constellations' reactions and muttered.
[What? What's everyone's problem? They look good together!]

The constellations on the first floor merely looked up at us in silence, admiration and worry mingling in their eyes. Both ‘Maritime War God’ and ‘Bald General of Justice’ looked tense, fearing trouble. Only ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ watched us with apparent interest.
As the laughter finally began to subside, more direct scorn flew down from the second floor.
[He hasn't even ascended to constellation status yet. What business does he have establishing a nebula?]
[Dokkaebi, does any of this make sense?]
[Does he think just any nobody can establish a nebula?]
The dokkaebi was visibly flustered by the barrage of questions.
[Well······ incarnation Kim Dokja has indeed had his ‘Status’ recognized by the <Star Stream>.]
With those words, the Stories I had achieved so far were projected onto the screen on the ceiling.
<King of a Kingless World>
The first scene to appear was of me borrowing the power of the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword to destroy the [Absolute Throne]. Strictly speaking, that was where my Story had begun.
Craaaack!
Fragments of the shattered throne scattered across the screen. Some constellations nodded as if making an effort to accept it, while others looked at one another in apparent horror.
[He destroyed a throne inhabited by an Outer God!]
[······Did he really begin his Story with that?]
It seemed that some of the attendees didn't know much about me.
I had thought I was pretty famous by now, but apparently that wasn't enough yet.
Glancing nearby, I noticed that Russian kid from earlier staring at me blankly.
<One Who Opposes the Extraordinary>
I had gained my second Story by defeating Myung Ilsang, the returnee who had descended as a disaster.
[Some constellations express their goodwill toward you.]
Constellations had always disliked ‘returnees’, so naturally, it was a Story well suited to winning their favor.
Then puzzlement appeared on the constellations' faces.
[······What's that now?]

What appeared with my third Story was a scene of me beating up the intermediate dokkaebi Paul. Even I was a little surprised by that footage. I thought it was probably from when I had stepped forward to avenge Shin Yoosung······
They'd counted even that as a ‘Story’?
Gwaaack! Aaargh!
As the intermediate dokkaebi's screams rang out one after another, the flustered host fast-forwarded the footage. Complaints immediately spread among the constellations.
[Hey, what was that just now!]
[W-well. Haha, it seems we have the wrong footage.]
Contrary to the dokkaebi's words, however, a Story title appeared on the screen.
<One Who Showed Contempt for a Streamer>
At that Story title, booming laughter came from the stair landing.
‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ was laughing as he looked at me.
[So you're a madman! Hahahaha!]
Then the fourth Story title appeared.
<One Who Hunted the King of Disasters>

I had obtained it by hunting the shadow of the constellation [Yamata no Orochi] in [Peace Land]. Watching Orochi fall to the electric attack I unleashed with [Electrification], the constellations' jaws dropped.
[The shadow of a Narrative-grade constellation······.]
[He's already accumulated four Stories of Legendary grade or higher?]
Confusion spread among the constellations.
Eventually, the footage ended, and the dokkaebi spoke.
[In any case, for these reasons, incarnation Kim Dokja currently stands on the verge of ascending to constellation status. If he acquires his ‘fifth Story’ through this opportunity······.]
Those who knew I was aiming to become a constellation weren't flustered, but the constellations who hadn't known looked astonished.
[He's ascending to constellation status before Scenario 10 is even over?]
[That fellow, a new constellation······.]
Suddenly, I was the focus of intense stares.
Certainly, an event like this would be extraordinary even across the entirety of ‘Ways of Survival’.
Only a very few constellations or returnees had earned recognition from the <Star Stream> and acquired Status before Scenario 10 ended.
As the confusion deepened, the one who spoke up was Manu, ‘Founder of Humanity’, who had attended as <Vedas>' negotiating representative.
[I will acknowledge incarnation Kim Dokja's Status. But I cannot acknowledge this matter concerning a ‘nebula’. There are two problems here.]
The constellations focused on Manu's voice.
[First, we do not know whether incarnation Kim Dokja has sufficient means to pay. You are aware that establishing a nebula requires a minimum amount of capital, aren't you?]
“I have enough coins.”
My words caused another stir among the audience.
Manu narrowed his eyes suspiciously before continuing.
[That can be verified. The second problem is who will ‘support’ your nebula.]
I swallowed discreetly.
The real obstacle had finally arrived.
[Establishing a nebula requires the support of at least five constellations. Which constellations have given you their support?]
When I couldn't readily answer, Manu smirked.
[No, does your nebula even have a ‘name’ in the first place?]
I glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk, then said whatever came to mind.
“Our nebula's name is······ Kim Dokja’s Company······.”
“There is no name yet. And we will find supporters starting now.”
Unexpectedly, Yoo Joonghyuk interrupted me and stepped forward.
“Are there any constellations willing to support our nebula?”
Yet the audience gave no response to Yoo Joonghyuk's words. Manu smirked.
[I thought as much. You've only wasted our time. Dokkaebi. Continue the succession ceremony······.]
But then, someone raised a hand for the first time.
[Olympus's ‘Underworld’ will support your nebula.]
[Queen!]
An enraged Manu snarled at Persephone.
Persephone, in turn, unleashed a fierce aura.
[This is my decision. What objection do you have?]
Even with <Vedas> behind him, a constellation of Manu's caliber could not defy Persephone, Queen of the Underworld, alone. In the end, he turned his attention to the other constellations.
[Surely there won't be anyone else?]
[I support them.]
The voice from the seat of highest honor on the second floor startled the constellations once again.
Because it belonged to none other than ‘Great Sage, Heaven's Equal’.
[P-Prisoner of the Golden Headband?]
[Really? Are you serious?]
I nodded toward him in thanks. Great Sage, Heaven's Equal merely looked down at us, picking his ear with his shrunken Ruyi Jingu Bang as though it were all a nuisance.
[Oh, to hell with it······ Sorry, Scribe! I support them too!]
At last, even Uriel of <Eden> declared her support.
[And I'll name their nebula, too! Its name will be Forbidden······ Mmph, mmph!]
I could see the ninth-rank angels around her trying to stop her in alarm.
Whatever her intentions, I was grateful.
Now the remaining constellations were simply watching one another for cues.

The three constellations who had declared their support were all powerful enough not to care what others thought. But it was different from here on. Few beings would want to defy Manu, a Narrative-grade constellation, merely to help establish a new nebula.
Looking beside me, I saw that Yoo Joonghyuk seemed halfway resigned as well.
―It seems this is as far as we go.
······So were we going to be stopped here after all?
But I didn't mind.
―It's fine. The objective's been achieved.
―What?
―I wasn't expecting it to work anyway. What matters is buying time.
I had never intended to inherit any constellation's Story here in the first place.
And if things followed the ‘original novel’ as I remembered it, the ending of this ‘banquet’ was already determined.
That was when something unexpected happened.
[I, ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’, will support their nebula.]
Goryeo’s First Sword, the strongest Historical-grade constellation, had declared his support for us.
At that, the Historical-grade constellations who had been holding themselves back until now rose all at once.
[Then I, ‘Maritime War God’, will also······!]
[This ‘Bald General of Justice’ will not stand idly by either!]
As the symbols on the first floor began declaring their support one after another, even the dokkaebis looked deeply flustered, along with the constellations on the second floor.
[W-wait a moment! You can't simply declare your support so indiscriminately······!]
And the next moment.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ supports your nebula.]
Secretive Plotter?
Where on earth?
[You have acquired a temporary right to establish a ‘nebula’!]
······Could it be?
Rrrrrumble!
A thunderous roar engulfed the entire banquet hall, and space began to warp violently.
I looked up at the sky.
At last, the end of this banquet was approaching.
‘They’ had arrived.
[······This presence?]
[Everyone, stand back!]
Even those constellations looked tense. Then the sky warped dramatically, and powerful sparks began to fly. It was as though the sky were cracking and splitting apart.
[Great Hole].
The mysterious hole that appeared only when a scenario activated had suddenly emerged above the banquet hall. A startled Manu shouted.
[Outer Gods! How dare you come here! Do you know where you are!]
All the constellations growled and unleashed their respective auras.
Then a horrifying voice came from the hole in the sky.
Why... didn't you invite us?
Persephone and Uriel rushed over in an instant and covered my ears and Yoo Joonghyuk's.
It was to block the Outer Gods' True Voice. Perhaps because they stood in front of us, the pressure emanating from the hole diminished somewhat.
[I'm sorry, but the party is over. It's time for you to go back.]
[See you again next time!]

As Persephone and Uriel shouted, my body and Yoo Joonghyuk's were enclosed in transparent circles. The constellations' power had begun transporting our spiritual bodies through space. It seemed they were trying to save us from the horrifying battle that would soon erupt in the banquet hall.
But the Outer Gods were a little faster.
Wait...
[The Outer Gods are looking at you!]
[The Outer Gods are looking at you!]
At the last moment, I heard Uriel scream.
[Kim Dokja!]
Then pitch-black darkness covered my vision.
【Who are you?】
【One unrecorded in the wheel.】
【Could it be...】
【Is the ‘final story’ finally about to begin······.】
“Hey, is this the right place?”
“Is this really okay? What if those guys show up? They said Maritime Admiral and Pure-Hearted Steel come here all the time!”
“And isn't this that ‘hero's’ grave?”
A pitch-black night.
Several grave robbers had gathered over a gravestone erected in the middle of Gwanghwamun.
The grave robber Lee Dongpa frowned at his companions, who were already frightened.
“Pathetic bastards. Hero, my ass. Would a hero die this easily?”
Lee Dongpa had learned of the hero's existence only recently.
The ‘strongest man’, who had sacrificed his life to save Seoul.
Of course, Lee Dongpa didn't believe the rumor.
“Come on, dig! We don't have time. Before those bastards who went into Dark Castle come out!”
Most people were already participating in the ninth scenario, [Dark Castle].
But Lee Dongpa and the others had not joined the scenario.
After all, main scenarios were just festivals for the big shots.
“It's supposed to be a hero's grave. There's bound to be a good thing or two buried here, right?”
“Search the corpse too! He might have hidden something inside his body!”
“Fuck, they buried him deep as hell. Hey, put your back into it!”
The grave robbers rapidly dug into the ground.
Had about two hours passed?
“W-we've reached it!”
At last, their shovels reached the coffin lid.
With his heart pounding, Lee Dongpa opened the lid without letting his excitement show.
Inside the coffin lay a sleeping man in a white coat.
Lee Dongpa smirked.
“A hero? Hmph. More like Sleeping Beauty. An ugly one, at that.”
“Nice coat, though. Let's take that off first······.”
Grab!
“A-aaaaaagh!”
“W-what the······ Aaaaaagh!”
Lee Dongpa, startled as well, collapsed where he stood and trembled.
The hero, who had certainly been dead until a moment ago, was gripping a grave robber's shoulder.
Then the following messages rang in the ears of every being in Seoul.
[Someone has acquired five Stories.]
[A new constellation (星座) has been born in Seoul's night sky!]
It was already their fifth day since entering the first floor of [Dark Castle].
With the injured Lee Gilyoung on her back, Lee Jihye was running through Dark Castle's corridors alongside Shin Yoosung.
[Grade-5 demons, ‘Dark Trackers’, are pursuing you!]
“Run!”
Dodging a scythe thrust out by a Dark Tracker, Lee Jihye set [Demon Slaying] ablaze.
As the scattered blue flames of magic power burned in midair, Lee Jihye ran with the children as fast as she could.
“Damn it, doesn't [Taming] work on them?”
“······I can only tame monsters.”
“Fuck!”
Hurling every curse she knew, Lee Jihye fled for her life.
There were more than ten demons pursuing them, by a rough count.
Grade-5 demons were stronger than other monsters. With her abilities, even one would be difficult to handle, and on top of that, she was in an environment where she couldn't properly use her stigmas.
‘I shouldn't have come in.’

After Kim Dokja's death, the group's morale had collapsed completely. Having lost their central figure, the companions began acting separately. To make matters worse, with even Yoo Joonghyuk's whereabouts now uncertain, the ninth scenario, [Dark Castle], appeared.
When the scenario first began, the dokkaebi had said this.
[This scenario······. Hmm. Haha, you'll probably fail.]
Lee Jihye's reaction to those words had been different.
We'd fail?
The scenarios had always seemed impossible, and we had always overcome them.
So we would be able to do well this time, too.
That was what Lee Jihye had thought.
‘Let's go right now. Let's crush every last one of those bastards!’

She didn't know why she had been so hasty. Perhaps it had been guilt rather than confidence. Guilt over someone's death, which seemed as though it could be erased only by cutting down monsters and pushing herself to her limits.
Perhaps Lee Jihye hadn't been the only one.
Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, and all the other companions had felt a similar sorrow.
And so, to shake off that sorrow, they had hastily stepped into the scenario area.
Whatever anyone said, they were Seoul's rankers, its strongest incarnations.
But before long, she came to realize that the decision had been a mistake.
‘Fuck, this is impossible······ It's impossible.’
Lee Jihye's strength was ineffective in [Dark Castle].
The sword strikes of her [Kendo], which had surpassed level 7, barely worked, while the power of [Demon Slaying] only provoked the demons.
Her sword had broken long ago.
“Jihye-unnie!”

At Shin Yoosung's shout, Lee Jihye snapped back to her senses and dodged a [Dark Tracker]'s blade. She picked up whatever weapons the nearby incarnations had dropped and unleashed her skills indiscriminately. Using [Kendo], using [Ghost Walk].
“Unnie! Behind you!”
Zzzzzzt!
The Dark Tracker's dark fluid (暗液), spraying through the air.
Flap-flap! Grrrrk!

Lee Gilyoung's little insects flew in from somewhere, and the liquid hit them instead of Lee Jihye. The insects struggled in the black fluid, underwent grotesque cellular mutations, then exploded. Thanks to the time the insects bought her, Lee Jihye was lucky enough to land several solid blows on a [Dark Tracker].
“Aaaaaaaaah!”
Clang-clang! Slash-slash!
As her weapon broke, one [Dark Tracker]'s head flew off.
But there were still nine behind them.
And the [Dark Trackers] were merely child's play.
Far more frightening was the creature beyond the [Dark Trackers].
[Demon Viscount Noslocke]
An appearance like an enormous rhinoceros head set atop a human body.
Whenever that hulking figure approached, the fine hairs all over Lee Jihye's body quivered.
She had never seen a monster like that.

In terms of individual strength, it probably wasn't as powerful as the ‘Disaster of Floods’. But whereas the ‘Disaster of Floods’ had held her own power back, this demon viscount did nothing of the sort.
Moreover, the fact that Lee Jihye herself had grown stronger since then was now working against her.
Being able to recognize her opponent's strength only fueled her fear.
Lee Jihye drew her blade back and bit her lip.
Here, like this······.
[An ‘Ancient Magic Power Barrier’ has formed on the first floor of Dark Castle.]
“Unnie, let's go over there!”
A blue room that had formed at the end of the corridor.
It was the only place in this [Dark Castle] where they could rest.

Lee Jihye and the children ran toward the room with all their might and barely escaped the [Dark Trackers]' pursuit. Though the little space was less than two pyeong, somehow there was just enough room for the three of them to take shelter.
[You have entered the ‘Ancient Magic Power Barrier’. A special barrier will activate for 30 minutes.]
Without this safe zone, which activated only three times a day, Lee Jihye and the children might have lost their lives long ago.
Zzzzzzt!
The [Dark Trackers] groaned and recoiled as they touched the bluish barrier.
They tried several times to enter the barrier before retreating as though they had given up. But one of them was different.
“Why isn't that bastard leaving?”
The demon resembling a rhinoceros.
[Demon Viscount Noslocke] settled onto the floor a few meters away from them, as though he knew how this barrier worked.
“······I think he's waiting for us.”

The demon's long tongue swept over his lips. Like a gourmet waiting for a delicious meal to finish cooking, he watched Lee Jihye and Shin Yoosung. Shuddering under that chilling gaze, Shin Yoosung asked.
“What do we do now? There aren't any more monsters I can summon.”
“We still have 30 minutes. Let's think.”

As the barrier happened to have formed at the edge of the fortress, Lee Jihye could see the scenery outside through a window. A special barrier prevented them from leaving through it, but at least they could see out.
Gyaaaaaah!

Demons were pouring out of the entrance to [Dark Castle] that Lee Jihye and her companions had thrown open. Most were lesser demons, but even those were too much for ordinary incarnations. The demons of [Dark Castle] devoured and infected Seoul's incarnations.
Grrrrr······.

As a result, many of the demons she could see outside the fortress had originally been people she knew. Min Jiwon's Hwarang. Nirvana's Salvation Church followers. People she had passed by had all become demonic people, tearing into others and roaming the streets. It was all the result of her haste. If, if only she had been a little more careful.
[Didn't I tell you? The difficulty is on an entirely different level from anything you've faced so far.]
Hearing the dokkaebi's voice from the air, Lee Jihye realized something.
The reason she had survived until now wasn't that she was strong.
It was that she had been lucky.
‘Damn it! Damn it! You stupid bitch!’
It was too late to blame her own haste now.
The companions who had entered without any preparation had scattered throughout Dark Castle's maze, and these children were the only ones she had managed to find.
What had happened to the others?
She didn't know.
Perhaps they were all dead.
‘If only Master were here. No······ Not Master······.’
“If Dokja-hyung were here······.”
At Lee Gilyoung's voice behind her, Lee Jihye frowned.
“Don't talk nonsense, idiot. If you're hurt, just get some sleep.”
After a smack to the back of his head, Lee Gilyoung fell silent again, but unfortunately, there was another mouth.
“There's no way ajusshi is dead. I don't really understand it, but that's how I feel.”
She was already upset enough to go mad. Why did these kids keep bringing up someone who was dead?
“He croaked. Hurry up and forget that ugly face.”
But Shin Yoosung reacted unexpectedly to the words she had blurted out in anger.
“But I honestly don't understand. Everyone says ajusshi is ugly, but what exactly is ugly about him?”
Being asked that out of the blue left her a little flustered.

They had all been pushing ‘Kim Dokja is ugly’ like a slogan all this time (some constellations even gave them coins for it occasionally), so she had never particularly questioned Kim Dokja's ‘ugliness’.
“Well, the shape of his eyes and nose······ The overall balance, I guess······.”
The more Lee Jihye spoke, the more confused she felt. When she actually thought about it, she couldn't quite figure out what was ugly about Kim Dokja.
No, she couldn't even clearly recall Kim Dokja's face.
As though it were hidden behind a hazy mist······.
Or as though it were a face that hadn't been made yet······.
Why?
Why······ couldn't she remember his face clearly?
“A-anyway, he's not my type.”
“······You cried an awful lot at his funeral, considering that.”
“Obviously I was acting, idiot. The constellations gave me tons of coins then.”
[Several constellations ask Lee Jihye whether she really was acting.]
Lee Jihye bit her lip.
“You still have a long way to go, unnie. Looks aren't all there is to a person.”
“You little······.”
Lee Jihye glared at the top of Shin Yoosung's head for a moment, then sighed.
“······I know that much too.”
Her voice was so quiet it was barely audible.
Knowing something didn't mean being able to admit it all.
At least, Lee Jihye was still at that age.
She owed Kim Dokja so much.
And she had survived because of him.
She knew. She knew very well, but she didn't want to admit it.
She had wanted to hold on somehow, repay her debt, and brag about it.
To say: she, too······ was actually pretty useful, wasn't she?
But now that chance was gone forever.
[The ‘Ancient Magic Power Barrier’ has 1 minute remaining.]
When she snapped back to her senses, the barrier before her was wavering. The demon's smile had grown broader. Lee Jihye realized it was time.
“Yoosung. You can carry Gilyoung on your back, right? When I give the signal, take him and run.”
“What?”
“Listen to me.”
Saving someone didn't suit a person who had killed her friend to survive.
Even so, that was how she wanted to live.
Because that was what the dead man had taught her.
“Hurry! Ask someone else for help while you run! Before I drop dead!”
“······All right. Just hold on a little longer, unnie.”
There probably wasn't anyone else.
But she had to say that.
Otherwise, the child wouldn't leave.

The instant the barrier disappeared, Lee Jihye lunged forward. The startled demons flinched, but that was all. They quickly surrounded her and lunged at her. Blood spurted from her pale thighs and forearms.
Spurt, crack!
What if there had been a lake nearby?
No, if only she could at least reach her [constellation sponsor], with whom contact had been cut off for several days.
“······I don't want to die.”
The trajectories of her [Kendo] strikes, unleashed with all her strength, gradually began to falter.
The demons' smiles gleamed.
A tremendous impact struck the back of her head, and her vision lurched violently for an instant.
Lee Jihye muttered without realizing it.
“I want to live too······.”
Somehow, she felt as though something similar had happened before.
What had happened then?
Whoooooosh!
That was when light poured in from ahead.
The Dark Trackers' bodies were splitting in two.
As though the Messiah had descended. As though the waves were parting in two.
Boom-boom-boom-boom!

Lee Jihye watched the scene as though entranced. The instant the startled Demon Viscount Noslocke turned his head, a powerful current burst from his head in an explosion. A man stood on the path of light formed by those dazzling currents.
Lee Jihye stammered, unable to get the words out.
He was the person whose face she hadn't been able to remember.
He seemed to be saying something, but she couldn't hear him clearly.
And the next moment, the mist covering his face disappeared.
He was furious, tearing at the demon like an evil spirit.
For what? She didn't know.
But one thing was certain······.
This time, she could clearly see his ‘face’.
······Was that what ajusshi's face looked like?
[A constellation who does not yet have a name is looking at you.]
Hearing that message, Lee Jihye gave a little smile and toppled forward.
“······That thing earlier was about you, wasn't it, ajusshi?”
“What?”
“That new constellation in Seoul or whatever······.”
“Ah······ Well. Yes.”
I smiled wryly as I looked at the demon corpses strewn around us.
I had rushed over in alarm after seeing Lee Jihye in danger, but I seemed to have gone a little too far.
[Demon Viscount Noslocke].
This sinister creature resembling a rhinoceros was a demon who, in the original course of this round, raped countless incarnations and tore them to death.
Having subdued a demon of noble rank in no time, I felt anew just how much stronger I had become.
Lee Jihye spoke as though she felt deflated.
“He was incredibly strong······. Just how much stronger do you get when you become a constellation?”
“I didn't kill him with my own power. I borrowed some power from other Stories.”
“Other Stories?”
Turning around, I saw Noslocke, who was still breathing, looking up at me.
“One moment.”
Crunch!
I simply stamped my foot down, making Noslocke's head burst.
[You have slain a noble of the Demon Realm!]
[You have acquired 10000 coins!]
[You have acquired the item ‘Superior Demon’s Proof’.]
[The lesser races of the Demon Realm will feel fear in your presence.]
Normally, killing a demon would make an enemy of the ‘Demon King’ it followed, but this scenario was different.
All the demons appearing in the [Dark Castle] scenario were waiting for a new ‘master’, so no Demon King in particular would be angered by their deaths.
[Some constellations are astonished by your overwhelming martial prowess.]
[A considerable number of constellations question your probability.]
Certainly, they had reason to question the probability.
My strength now clearly violated the scenario's balance.
But the reason I had defeated ‘Noslocke’ so easily wasn't simply that I had become a ‘constellation’.
[Some effects of the Story <Messiah’s Path> are being applied.]
‘Absolute Holiness’, an effect of <Messiah’s Path>.
I had borrowed this Story, which was especially effective against demons, from <Eden>.
[The nebula <Eden> requests payment for your ‘Story citation’.]
Swish, swish.
As I traced the sign of the cross in the air, a message sounded.
[The nebula <Eden> is pleased by your ‘Story citation’.]
Doing what they wanted every time I repeated the ‘citation’ was a nuisance, but it was better than getting into a dispute over Story plagiarism.
Besides, this time they didn't ask for any other payment as long as I made the sign of the cross.
<Eden> had given me a special deal to celebrate my becoming a constellation.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is delighted!]
It was all thanks to adorable Uriel.
Fortunately, things at the ‘banquet’ seemed to have worked out.
“Ajusshi······ Did you find religion while you were gone?”
Lee Jihye laughed between ragged breaths.
Through-and-through wounds and stab wounds in her right shoulder and lower abdomen.
“Sorry. I'm supposed to be ranked 10th in Seoul, but I look pretty pathetic, don't I?”
“This is the hardest stretch for you. Things will get better from here, so don't worry. All right, I'm going to set your bones now. Stay still.”
